title: Disaster restore proof
description: Objective: prove complete backup generations, two-slot recovery anchors, fresh incarnation/key epochs, orphan inventory, and quiesced recovery after media loss. Deliverable: CORE-S14 restore fixtures and evidence. NOT in scope: ordinary restart or optimistic orphan adoption. Hard dependencies: full store/artifact/effect inventory implementations. Owned paths: tests/fault/disaster-restore/** and backup tooling paths. Verification: pnpm test:fault.
definitionOfDone: Crash at every prepare/install/fsync/switch boundary exposes either old authority or one verified quiesced restore, never a mixture.
Repeated same-generation restore uses fresh incarnation/key epochs and all stale grants fail.
Missing inventory or artifact/key proof keeps recovery unavailable with UNKNOWN_TRUTH.
taskRails: Claims follow the benchmark permit-list; missing, partial, cross-basis, or unverifiable evidence is UNKNOWN, never PASS.
No confirmatory corpus is generated or viewed until the implementation commit is frozen exactly as specified.
GO_QUIESCE and GO_ACTIVATE are separate human decisions. Keep evidence exact, reproducible, and scoped to one source commit.

implementationPlan.description: DoD 1 — CRASH AT EVERY BOUNDARY. Create tests/fault/disaster-restore/anchor-boundary-crash.fault.ts. Production enumerates EIGHT boundaries, all confirmed live call sites: PREPARE (packages/store/src/recovery-anchor.ts:83 and :95), then INACTIVE_INSTALL, TRANSACTION, FILE_FSYNC, DIRECTORY_PERSISTENCE, VERIFICATION, SWITCH, INSTALLED_MARKER (packages/store/src/recovery-anchor-install.ts:232-260). Write the eight names OUT BY HAND in this file as a frozen literal, then assert set-equality in BOTH directions against the imported `RECOVERY_ANCHOR_FAULT_POINTS` and assert the swept case count is exactly 8. Hand-written plus production-compared is deliberate: a table derived from the enum cannot police the enum, and a hand list alone silently under-sweeps when production grows a ninth point. For each of the 8: seed a generation, install a first anchor cleanly so an OLD authority exists, then attempt a second same-project install with `crashAt(point)` and catch CrashSignal. Then, using ONLY production readers, assert the post-crash world is one of exactly two admissible states and never a blend — (A) OLD AUTHORITY: `inspectRecoveryAnchor` reports the pre-crash record with its original currentSlot and original anchorDigest, and `verifySlot` over that still-current slot passes; or (B) ONE VERIFIED QUIESCED RESTORE: `inspectRecoveryAnchor` reports state INSTALLED, and `verifySlot` over the NEW currentSlot passes, and the record carries restoredLifecycle QUIESCED / restoredReadiness RECOVERY_REQUIRED / restoredAuthorityRevoked true. Assert the mixture is absent explicitly, not by omission: it is never true that currentSlot moved while `verifySlot` over it fails, and never true that state is INSTALLED while the slot is unverifiable. Assert the exact boundary-to-outcome mapping per point rather than an or-of-eight, so a point that silently changes side turns this file red. Also assert that after every crash the only permitted operations are `RECOVERY_ANCHOR_ALLOWED_OPERATIONS` (INSPECT, RESUME, DISCARD) — drive `resumeRecoveryAnchor` and require it either completes to a verified INSTALLED state or refuses with a pinned `RECOVERY_ANCHOR_REASON_CODES` member AND its `layer`, never merely 'not ok'. CROSS-PLATFORM: packages/store/src/recovery-anchor-fs.ts:18 sets DIRECTORY_FSYNC_SUPPORTED = process.platform !== 'win32'. The DIRECTORY_PERSISTENCE fault point still FIRES on Windows (the callback runs before the platform check), so the case is swept everywhere — but do NOT assert POSIX directory-durability side effects; assert only the two admissible states above, which hold on all three platforms.

implementationPlan.description: DoD 2 — FRESH EPOCHS ON REPEAT, STALE GRANTS FAIL. Create tests/fault/disaster-restore/restore-identity-epochs.fault.ts. Restore the SAME backup generation twice (identical generationDigest — assert that equality explicitly so the 'same generation' premise is pinned and cannot silently become two generations). Mint each restore identity through the production service: `createRecoveryIncarnationService` with `createNodeRecoveryCryptoPort`, both from the @moe/daemon bare specifier. Assert the second restore's incarnationRef differs from the first AND its keyEpochRef differs from the first — assert BOTH separately; they are one atomic fencing identity and a test that checks only the nonce passes while the key epoch is reused. Anchor each with `anchorIncarnation` and read back with `readAnchoredIncarnation`, asserting the second read returns the second incarnation and that its backupGenerationDigest still equals the shared generation digest (fresh identity, same generation — that is the whole point). STALE GRANTS: drive the first (now superseded) incarnationRef/keyEpochRef against the post-second-restore world through the exported production surfaces — `readSuccessionChain` for the chain verdict and `runRecoveryCompleteCommand` for the command verdict — and assert the SPECIFIC stable reason code plus WHICH LAYER answered, never merely that it failed. Candidate codes live in RECOVERY_SUCCESSION_ERROR_CODES / RECOVERY_COMPLETION_CODES / RECOVERY_INCARNATION_ERROR_CODES, all exported from @moe/daemon; pin the member the surface actually returns and pin its layer constant, because more than one layer can refuse here and 'refused' alone is one added layer away from vacuous. Also cover the mirror case — a stale key epoch paired with a CURRENT incarnation — so the fence is proven on both operands rather than on their conjunction. HARD CONSTRAINT: if the exported surface genuinely cannot express a stale grant, do NOT reimplement the fence in the test and do NOT narrow the DoD — call moe.report_blocked naming the missing symbol.

implementationPlan.description: DoD 3 — MISSING PROOF KEEPS RECOVERY UNAVAILABLE AS UNKNOWN_TRUTH. Create tests/fault/disaster-restore/recovery-unknown-truth.fault.ts. Cover three distinct absences, each its own case, and assert the code AND the layer for each — production pins the coordinator answer to UNKNOWN_TRUTH at layer RECOVERY_INVENTORY (packages/../apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-inventory-contract.ts:24 and :268), and the contract comment at durable-recovery-inventory-contract.ts:153 warns that several upstreams collapse to the same code, so the upstream tuple is what distinguishes them: assert it, not just the code. Case 1 — NO INVENTORY: `readRecoveryReconciliation` with no recorded reconciliation returns UNKNOWN_TRUTH at RECOVERY_INVENTORY. Case 2 — MISSING ARTIFACT PROOF: record a reconciliation whose item lacks its artifact proof, then `readRecoveryCompletionEvidence` returns UNKNOWN_TRUTH (see apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-completion-evidence.ts:368 for the production site) with the upstream naming the artifact gap. Case 3 — MISSING KEY PROOF: same shape with the key-epoch proof absent. In EVERY case then drive `runRecoveryCompleteCommand` and assert recovery stays UNAVAILABLE — a pinned RECOVERY_COMPLETION_CODES member plus its layer — so the test proves the absence actually WITHHOLDS authority rather than merely that a reader said UNKNOWN. Assert the negative too: no project lifecycle transition out of QUIESCED occurred and no recovery.complete event was appended, read back from the store. Do NOT let a shape-validation refusal stand in for a truth refusal: build each fixture so it is VALID at every earlier layer and only the target proof is absent, otherwise an earlier guard answers first and the assertion quietly detaches from its subject.

implementationPlan.description: DoD 4 — RUN THE GATE AND PROVE IT EXECUTED. Three legs, each run SEPARATELY with its own exit code captured (never `;`-chained, never piped into tail — a pipe reports tail's exit code and a semicolon reports only the last command's). LEG 1, scoped executed-count proof: `npx vitest run --config tests/fault/vitest.config.ts disaster-restore` from the repo root.
